Commentary.Commentary: It's never easy to bat last in a Test match. England have a target of 283 to overhaul and they have to deal a quality bowling attack of Pakistan. They would hope that they start well against the new ball. Stay tuned, England will start their chase shortly.

Pakistan would have liked to bat better in this innings but plenty of their batsmen got starts and then faltered. Asad Shafiq, Sarfraz Ahmed and Yasir Shah added vital runs to the lead and the visitors will be backing themselves to defend this total. Having said that, they would have loved to get somewhere near 350.

Right then, England didn't take much time to polish Pakistan's tail. Stuart Broad picked up both the remaining wickets but once again the star with the ball for the English team was Chris Woakes who finished with 11 wickets in this Test match.

OUT! Amir departs! Broad gets another wicket in his second over of the morning! Length ball outside off, it goes straight after pitching. Amir looks to cut that hard but gets a thick outside edge and Bairstow makes no mistakes as he takes yet another catch. So, Pakistan are all out on 215 and England will have to chase 283 to win.

Stuart Broad becomes the first bowler to take 350 wickets in minimum innings in Tests. Can England get Pakistan wrapped up under 300 now?

Hello and welcome back for Day 4 of this first Test match of this series at Lord's. The game is nicely positioned at this stage where both teams are in with a chance, however Pakistan have an upper hand. The visiting side is surely looking in a great shape after having a decent lead of 281 and would like to add on it this morning with 2 wickets in hand. The home side will like to execute their plans better on this crucial day as this will be a deciding day of the match in all likelihood. Let's anticipate a great game ahead.
DAY 4... SESSION 1

Going into Day 4, Pakistan will be well and truly on top. With still 2 wickets in hand, it will be interesting to see what Misbah-ul-Haq will do tomorrow. Will he declare early and try to go for the jugular tomorrow itself? Or let his side play this one out? They have a good lead and certainly have the bowlers in their arsenal to defend it. Do join us for it, folks. The action on Day 4 begins at 1530 IST tomorrow. Till then, take care and be well!

The English bowlers had the opportunity to claw their way back. Particularly when the visiting team's skipper was dismissed for a duck, but couldn't capitalize on it. They let partnerships build in the middle and that led to their downfall, a couple of dropped catches didn't do them any good either. Though towards the end, some magic produced from Woakes did give them something to take from the day. He picked up his second 5-fer and his first ever 10-wicket haul in Test cricket. A truly phenomenal feat.

Then two solid partnerships towards the end, first between Shafiq and Sarfraz, and then Sarfraz and Yasir Shah, really put the tourists in prime position. The Pakistan players will have gleeful smiles on their faces as they look at the scoreboard and see how well they've fared today.

The day started with Pakistan wrapping England up in under 9 overs. Then they were playing well, when Woakes continued his exceptional form. Along with Broad, got the top order out in quick succession and got England back into the game somewhat, Misbah's wicket really would have solidified their stance. But then Younis and Shafiq played really well, in particular the latter who took charge of things. Weaving a partnership of 69 runs, they ensured their team got into a great position.

32 overs, 103 runs and 4 wickets - An entertaining session to say the least, don't you think? Pakistan have finished the day on 214/8 and now lead by 281 runs. A day which has well and truly belonged to the visiting side.

DAY 3... SESSION 3...
So meet you all after the Tea break for the last session of day 3 and see who ends up on the top after the day's play.

English bowlers bowled well, maintaining a good line and length. Especially Woakes who continued his good rhythm to add on his strong performance in the first innings. Asad Shafiq and Younis Khan's half century stand at the end steadied the Pakisatni ship. They will hope to have a good last session and end the day on a high note.

DAY 3... SESSION 2...

Mohammad Hafeez and Shan Masood got Pakistan off to a slow start as the English bowlers came out with a vengence. Stuart Broad drew first blood early on as he removed Hafeez for a duck. However, the arrival of Azhar Ali provided a steadying influence and he and Masood have maintained a  solid partnership. After lunch, the two batsmen would like to dig themselves in more comfortably and build up on their lead. Join us for the second session on Day 3.

The first session has belonged to Pakistan. They have lost just one wicket and look well set right now. Pakistan was off to a good start to the day, mowing through England's lower order batsmen and ending the innings in just over 8 overs. England ended the 2nd innings on 272 and trailed by 67 runs.

NOT OUT! That's England's review gone! Pitched on middle and off, Azhar steps across and looks to flick it. The ball spins onto Azhar's pads and is flighted to the fielder at short leg. A massive appeal goes up but the umpire is not impressed. The English side confer for a bit and decide to review it. The replay clearly shows that there was no contact with the bat on either hotspot or snicko and the batsman is safe.
